Diary line at the first trap: a torn pasture-test tag was caught beneath the spring. Its number belongs to a drum the return ledger calls sealed.

There was a place for a signature and no one willing to write one. I used the margin to note what we actually found.

I do not know which of the two accounts was repeated afterward. The older one is the one I had in my hands that day.

Road-crew receipt: barriers were moved downhill after a trial drum leaked. The billed time is two hours before the radio announced an emergency route.

I set it aside to show the neighbor when she returned. Her porch was empty by the time the light was good enough to read it.

There may be a simple reason for the change. Nobody at the next stop could tell us what to do with the first version.
